results.summary_before: This design implements an IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 engine with polynomial 0xEDB88320, an 8-byte FIFO, and a one-bit-per-cycle serial processing path. It exposes a bidirectional register read interface with write, read, address, enable, and reset controls, plus an interrupt output, and it renders FIFO occupancy, FSM state, and all 32 CRC bits on a VGA display across two grid rows. A TinyVGA PMOD is required for the visual output, and a microcontroller such as an Arduino or RP2040 drives the input and bidirectional data buses. The project targets edge AI data-integrity use cases and runs in a single clock domain at 25 MHz.

results.summary_before: This project displays the Hackerspace Trójmiasto logo on a VGA monitor at 640x480 resolution. It includes a VGA timing generator and a bitmap ROM for the logo, with configurable color modes and animation such as bouncing or tiling. The design requires an external PMOD-to-VGA adapter to connect to a standard monitor. It is part of the IEEE Open-Silicon initiative and is fully synthesizable for ASIC implementation.

results.summary_before: This is a 4-bit password security system that grants access for a correct code and triggers a persistent alarm for the trap code 1111. It uses combinational logic for comparison and an SR latch so that the alarm state remains active until a manual reset, demonstrating both combinational and sequential logic in hardware security. The design is implemented in Wokwi. To test it, DIP switches provide the 4-bit input, and LEDs (red and green) plus a buzzer indicate access granted or alarm states. External hardware includes an 8-position DIP switch, pushbuttons for step and reset, LEDs, a buzzer, and resistors. The documentation notes that the circuit processes an 8-bit input in the description despite the 4-bit title, which may be a inconsistency.

results.summary_before: This design is a digital physical unclonable function (PUF) that uses eight distinct-tap maximal-length 10-bit LFSRs as virtual ring oscillators. A 6-bit challenge selects a pair of LFSRs, and an arbiter compares their popcounts over a programmable window to produce a response bit. 64 challenges accumulate into a 64-bit response, which can be XORed with a host-loaded memristor vector for dual-entropy mode. It is SPI-programmable and requires no external hardware, though an SPI master is needed for configuration.

results.summary_before: This design generates a VGA test pattern resembling NTSC color bars, with optional station ID display, scrolling ID, and scrolling bars. It is configured through input pins for showing the ID, using a custom ID, scrolling the ID, and scrolling the bars, and it outputs RGB and sync signals on the Tiny VGA pinout. A TinyVGA PMOD is required to connect to a VGA monitor, and the colors are explicitly not accurate to real NTSC color bars. Silicon test reports indicate it works, though one tester noted the clock must be manually set to 25 MHz in the commander app.
